decision.explanation: The provided evidence from pmid-25669829 directly supports the claim. The study reports that in patients with advanced solid tumors, specifically in the subgroup of metastatic colorectal cancer, the presence of hotspot TP53 mutations (including TP53 R213*, TP53 G245S, and TP53 R273C) was associated with improved clinical outcomes when treated with the combination of pazopanib and vorinostat. Specifically, patients with these mutations had significantly longer median progression-free survival (6.5 months vs 2.0 months) and overall survival (19.8 months vs 7.2 months) compared to those without the mutations. The evidence explicitly lists the specific variants mentioned in the claim and confirms the direction of effect (improved PFS and OS) for the specified therapy combination in the specified disease context.

citations.quote:
In the phase I study of pazopanib and vorinostat in 36 patients with advanced solid tumors, detection of hotspot TP53 mutation was associated with a higher rate of SD ≥6 months/PR, longer median PFS (months), and longer median OS (months) compared to patients without a hotspot TP53 mutation. 
In colorectal cancer cases, detected TP53 hotspot mutations included TP53 R213*, TP53 G245S, and TP53 R273C.

In the subgroup of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and sarcoma treated with pazopanib and vorinostat, those with detected hotspot TP53 mutations (n = 6) had a significantly longer median PFS of 6.5 months (95% CI 3.0–9.0; p = 0.023) compared to 2.0 months (95% CI 1.8–2.2; p = 0.023) in TP53-undetected cases (n = 10), and a significantly longer median OS of 19.8 months (95% CI 8.2–31.4; p = 0.021) versus 7.2 months (95% CI 0.6–13.8; p = 0.021), respectively.

findings.statement: The combination of pazopanib and vorinostat is associated with improved progression-free survival and overall survival in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer harboring hotspot TP53 mutations, including the specific variants TP53 R213*, TP53 G245S, and TP53 R273C.
